newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mounting political worries hit French stocks.
newsitem.headline: Mounting political worries hit French stocks.

text.p: Mounting speculation about the prospect of an early parliamentary election drove French shares down sharply at Friday's opening but investors were not yielding to panic, brokers said.
The market is also likely to remain volatile over the next few days as operators await to see if the parliament might be dissolved, they said.
"There is some selling. But absolutely no panic. People are just being cautious due to political uncertainties," one broker said.
The CAC-40 blue chip index was off 2.14 percent at 2,559.23 points at 0922 GMT, having opened down 1.19 percent.
Another broker said some investors were worried the dissolution of parliament might pave the way for a new austerity plan in France ahead of the euro single currency.
"There is some concern over a new austerity plan and its possible impact on economic growth," one broker said.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Friday he had confidence in the government's growth, public deficit and social security deficits forecasts.
"I'd like to say to you, and repeat to you, that public spending is under control and the government will meet the 3 percent target... and 2.8 percent in 1998," Arthuis said at a news conference.
One share dealer said that French and foreign fund managers were hedging their bets ahead of what could be a "very hot" weekend.

"Everyone is very calm. There seems to be a consensus at this stage that there will be a dissolution of parliament. But there are still questions about the timing of the announcement," one dealer said.
He also said there was talk an announcement could be made this weekend.
There has been so far no clear cut denial of the rumours President Jacques Chirac could announce either a reshuffle or an early election, possibly next week.
The only official comment from Chirac's office so far simply said the rumours were "without" foundation although the presidential source added "The president has time on his hands for reflection."
